newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures surge to huge daily gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures surge to huge daily gains.

text.p: News that U.S. budget negotiators finally hammered out a pact reinvigorated buyers of U.S. stock index futures, which sprinted to hefty daily gains.

Budget documents show the outline agreement, which needs Congressional passage, would reduce taxes by a net $85 billion over five years and cut the capital gains tax, provide relief for expanded IRA accounts and slow medicare spending growth.

June Standard & Poor's 500 futures, which already held large gains, rallied nearly an additional eight points during the final budget-inspired runup that began minutes after U.S. Treasury bond futures closed firm.

Brokers said the surge saw longs pile in and shorts, some of whom had taken short-term positions when the rally paused, scurry out in heavy volume trading estimated on the price boards at 90,000 contracts in June S&P 500s alone.

One floor broker said S&P 500s rallied "with authority." He also noted that other indices such as the Midcap 400 and Russell 2000 finally showed signs of catching up to the S&P 500's rise, while the NASDAQ 100 index rocketed higher.
"It was crazy," he said, remembering that two days ago his firm's floor chartist had forecast a possible test of the 820.00 level soon for nearby S&P 500 futures.

"Even our technician is looking at it (rally) and saying it has no rhyme or reason to it," he added. "It's strong. It's not heavy at all...(but) we are definitely on the fence again. Monday we'll either get a correction or head higher again."
The next obvious levels are near 819.05, the March 11 settlement, and at 822.70, the March 10 settlement.
Futures rose early with U.S. Treasury bond futures and on optimism that the ostensibly weak April U.S. jobs report might not shove the Federal Reserve into another tightening May 20.
But closer examination of the data took some of the positive spin out of the headline figures, brokers said.
Non-farm payrolls last month rose 142,000, with construction and manufacturing jobs declining. The jobless rate slid to 4.9 percent, its lowest level in 23 years.
Average hourly earnings fell 0.08 percent, while the average workweek shrank to 34.6 hours.
Futures moved little when final April University of Michigan consumer sentiment was reported at 101.4 or when March U.S. leading indicators rose 0.1 percent.

June S&P 500s rallied 14.50 pts to 816.55, Value Lines surged 17.70 to 723.75, Nikkei rose 380.0 to 19,690.0, Russell gained 9.60 to 358.85, and NASDAQ soared 28.85 pts to 917.85. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
